result: `PostController.destroy` was the only mutating action that skipped the gate — it looked up the post and deleted it without consulting `PostPolicy`, even though `PostPolicy.delete` (which already restricts deletion to the post's author) was registered in `AuthorizationProvider` and `update`/`edit` both call `this.authorize`. I added `await this.authorize('delete', [Post, post])` in `app/Http/Controllers/PostController.ts` immediately after `Post.findOrFail(id)` and before `Post.delete(...)`, matching the shape of `update`; the route is already behind the `auth` middleware, so guests still get the usual redirect to `/login` and a signed-in non-author now gets a `403` with the post intact. I also added `tests/PostAuthorization.test.ts`, a feature test that migrates the test SQLite database, creates two users and a post, and asserts that a non-author gets `403` and the post survives, a guest is refused and the post survives, and the author can still delete their own post. `bun run typecheck` and `bun test` (5 tests across 3 files) both pass.
